title: Starting clarinet: solfege with his father, then Lorenzo Tio Jr.
summary: His father taught solfege first, Manuel Perez was his godfather, and he began clarinet on a C clarinet with young Lorenzo Tio.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: He began with the old method, which often you've heard before, with the solfege. It was singing and for ear training. And then after when he thought I was ready to start on the instrument, then he sent me to Lorenzo Tio Jr.

But how long did he work with you on the solfege? The workman was just about nine months. I know Manuel Perez, they say, did that. And the Tio's too would make you sing a long time. And incidentally speaking, Manuel Perez, he is my godfather. Oh, is that right? Yeah, my godfather. Yes, right. He was my godfather. And by the way, the clarinet then was your first instrument? It is. Yeah, the clarinet was my first instrument. Did you ever want to take up drums? Or were you ever curious about them when your father had them around the house? Well, a little curious, but it was so much to love with. That's why I didn't want to buy it. No, no, baby.
And when I first began on the clarinet, because of my fingers being short, I had to use a C clarinet.
Like Big Eye Louie, I guess, used for a long time, they say. Mm.

Yeah. They weren't long enough to expand over the B flat on, or the A clarinet, because they were using those too at the same time. So it was a clarinet of Tio's, but he started off on his C. It was the C-inch.
Is that the young Lorenzo Tio, not the old? No, it's the young Lorenzo. The power, the other older teacher.
No, it wasn't the uncle or the father. It was the young Lorenzo Tio.
